name: Azure AI Search
tagline: Microsoft's managed search service for full-text, vector, hybrid and agentic retrieval on Azure.
description: Azure AI Search (formerly Azure Search, then Azure Cognitive Search) is a fully managed retrieval service on Azure. It indexes JSON documents with inverted and vector indexes, adds hybrid ranking with a semantic reranker, and can chunk and vectorize content during indexing through skillsets and Azure OpenAI. Its newer agentic retrieval mode plans and fans out sub-queries over knowledge bases, and it underpins Foundry IQ for Microsoft Foundry agents. Pick it when your data and identity already live in Azure; it is not available elsewhere.

pricing.notes: Free tier for small indexes; dedicated tiers bill per search unit (partitions x replicas) per hour. A serverless pricing model is in preview. Semantic ranker and agentic retrieval are billed separately.

scale.notes: Scale by adding partitions (storage) and replicas (QPS/HA). Multi-region requires separate services kept in sync by your indexers.

strengths: Integrated vectorization: chunk and embed during indexing with Azure OpenAI
Hybrid search with a semantic reranker built in
Agentic retrieval over multiple knowledge sources for agents
Indexers pull from Blob, Cosmos DB, SharePoint, OneLake and SQL
Entra ID RBAC, Private Link and document-level security trimming
weaknesses: Tier sizing and per-feature charges make costs hard to predict
Index schema changes often require full rebuilds
Less control over ranking internals than self-hosted engines
useCases: Enterprise RAG over SharePoint and Blob content
Site and catalog search on Azure
Hybrid semantic search for internal knowledge bases
